title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents
summary: SCALE replaces transmission of full latent messages or raw sensor data between cyber-physical agents with a scheduler that reuses matched tokens from prior messages and transmits only a budgeted subset of latent tokens chosen by profiled semantic gain versus communication cost. It costs an online token-matching stage, per-message semantic/cost profiling, and a real-time scheduling component, plus an anonymous-repository codebase whose maturity is unverified; quality degrades gracefully only insofar as the profiles are accurate. It can fail when scene dynamics break the assumed spatio-temporal continuity (making token reuse stale or wrong), when semantic-gain profiles misestimate task utility under shifting deadlines, or when the reader's workload is LLM-agent orchestration rather than bandwidth-constrained embodied multi-agent communication.
rationale: The method targets networked cyber-physical and robotic agents with heterogeneous deadlines, a setting an ML engineer on a single 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs is unlikely to operate, so it warrants monitoring rather than adoption or small-scale testing.
technique: Bandwidth-aware latent token scheduling for cyber-physical agents
